newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end down, further falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end down, further falls seen.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Wednesday as the maturation of a total of T$15 billion worth of treasury bills eased banking system liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate finished at 6.929 percent against Tuesday's 7.011 close -- still far outside the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper also falling to 6.75 percent against 6.85.
Dealers expected further falls on Thursday as money which flew out of the banking system earlier this month were continuing to return.
The central bank's issuance of T$5 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit only absorbed a small portion of excess funds in the banking system, dealers said.
The interbank rate is expected to waver around 6.850-875 on Thursday.

In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 government bond yields were traded at 6.0903-0905 percent against Tuesday's 6.0900 close. Dealers expected a continued consolidation as many investors remained on the sidelines due to the lack of significant market-inspiring news.
